chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) read me something from the book of Ali (peace be upon him), and it contained: 'He forbids you from the Jirriyth, al-Zimmir, al-Marmahi, al-Tafi, and al-Tihal.' I said, 'May Allah have mercy on you, we are brought fish that have no skin/scales.' He said, 'Eat what has skin/scales from the fish, and do not eat what has no skin/scales.'

key_terms.الزِّمِّيرِ: A type of fish, often identified as a type of carp or similar freshwater fish
key_terms.الطَّافِي: A type of fish, often identified as a type of catfish or similar
key_terms.الطِّحَالِ: A type of fish, often identified as a type of mullet or similar
key_terms.الْجِرِّيثِ: A type of fish, often identified as sturgeon or a specific freshwater fish
key_terms.الْمَارْمَاهِي: A type of fish, often identified as a type of sea bream or similar
key_terms.قِشْرٌ: Skin or scales (referring to the outer covering of the fish)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on eating fish without scales?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing edible fish by the presence of scales (qishr), a ruling traced back to Imam Ali (AS) via the chain of Alaa ibn al-Hadrami and Muhammad ibn Muslim. It addresses the practical application of dietary laws by clarifying that fish lacking scales are prohibited, thereby resolving ambiguities regarding specific marine species encountered in daily life.
